Description: Clean HUD & menus: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
Replace the native HUD. Off restores it immediately.
Show water, food and sleep beneath HP and armor.
Show HP and armor values inside their bars.
Show insanity in the top right while above zero.
Compass icons and distances for vehicle groups: merchants yellow, Coyotes green, patrols red and convoys orange.
Compass icons and distances for native locations within 1 km.
Show multiplayer teammates, their names and distances on the Wild Wasteland compass. This is your own display preference.
Show colored direction arrows for all multiplayer players, including you, on the map. This is your own HUD preference.
Show all compass vehicle groups with white vehicle icons, keeping their distances.
Show undiscovered compass locations as neutral question marks. Approaching within 100 m or spotting through binoculars remembers their real icons and colors. Quest flags are unchanged.
Show the compass, including its direction strip and all markers.
Show the gear/RPM/speed HUD only while driving in third person. Off allows either camera view; the source HUD enable switch still applies.
HUD scale; each panel grows away from its screen edge.
Enable the native debug map on the game's Map key.

Off hides map markers; Ambiguous shows question marks until locations are discovered within 100 m or spotted through binoculars; On shows their icons and colors. Discoveries are saved. Map icons have no name labels.

World traffic markers: moving dots and names of patrols, convoys, merchants and foot travelers. Off hides them; Ambiguous shows gray Unknown; On shows their colors and names. Independent of location markers; fog of war still applies.
Route lines of world traffic only (the moving markers are World traffic markers). Off hides them; Ambiguous draws them gray; On in faction colors.
Hide the parts of the map you have not explored yet. Exploring is recorded while this is off.
Share explored map areas with everyone in the multiplayer world. Off restores each player's personal exploration, which keeps recording while sharing is on. Controlled by the host.
Base range in meters. Exploration reveals twice this radius; high ground extends it up to threefold (4 km radial cap), with raised binoculars doubling the viewed cone again.
Width in meters of the soft edge, measured inward from the reveal radius. 0 = hard edge.
1 hides unexplored areas completely; lower values leave them faintly visible.
Remembered additional binocular magnification. Scroll while binoculars are raised to change it from 1x to 2x.
Replace the title and pause menus with CleanHUD's menus.
Use CleanHUD's forcedSquare font instead of the game's Helveticrap font. Applies to CleanHUD and its settings text.
CleanHUD text and border accent; also selectable at the bottom of the title and pause menus.
Add the game's cheat controls to the menu settings.
Detailed info logging for every module (off for normal play).
Show Developer while Enable Debug is on. Contains advanced settings, editors and diagnostics.
Show optional mod recommendations at the title menu.
Engine Sim compatibility: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
Guns, ammo & tracers: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.

Real bullets for NPC and player guns: flight time, falloff with distance, headshots and vehicle part damage. Off = the game's own instant hits; the NPC module controls NPC decisions separately. (Gunplay: [General] EnableGunplay)
Every physical gun keeps its own magazine and chamber state (saved with the game). Off = the game's own shared ammo per gun type; magazines are not saved while off.
Hold Reload to unload the current gun. Short presses reload on release. Per-gun magazines remain tracked when this is off. (Gunplay: [Ammo] EnableUnloading)
Drop excess ammo when switching to a smaller backpack or removing it. Failed drops retain the ammo and retry. (Gunplay: [Ammo] DropBackpackOverflow)

Drop one armor plate for each full 50 points of excess armor when switching to lower-capacity body armor. Excess below 50 produces no plate. Failed drops retain armor and retry. (Gunplay: [Ammo] DropArmorOverflow)
Adjust the health of the human bosses (Duke Ironjaw, Buzzgut) to [Guns / Bosses] AdjustHumanBossHP. Off = the game's own boss health.

Projectiles of monsters without guns (Arachnid, Teacher and the like) are stopped by walls, terrain and vehicles; car glass, grids, doors and plates let them through as often as a pistol bullet. Off = the game's own projectiles, which fly through everything. Needs Projectiles.

Your melee weapons hit wheels hard (x [Guns / Ballistics] WheelDamageMultiplier), also fitted wheels the game's own swing passes through; a wheel brought to 0 pops off (WheelPopOff). Off = the game's own melee damage on wheels (the Patrols module's simpler fitted-wheel melee takes over).
NPC gunmen aim at the centre of your body and lead moving targets (tuning in F7 > Weapons & HUD > NPC aim). Off = the game's own aim point (your head) and no lead. Needs Projectiles.
First person: while aiming down sights, scroll up to zoom in smoothly and down to zoom out. Up to 3x additional zoom, including scopes. Leaving sights resets the zoom.
Press Aim Down Sights once to aim and again to stop aiming. Off: hold the button as in the original game.
First person: lower the current weapon and raise the next weapon smoothly when drawing, holstering or switching slots.
Seconds to hold Reload before unloading; a shorter press reloads on release.
Health of the human bosses (Duke Ironjaw 1500, Buzzgut 600) in % of the game's own.
Bullet speed, m/s.
Crossbow bolt speed, m/s.
Damage of a bullet in the head - yours on NPCs, NPCs' on you and on each other (replaces the game's own x2 on NPC heads).
Draw the glowing trail of every bullet in flight (crossbow bolts are always drawn).
Draw tracers for your own shots too.
Bullets damage the vehicle parts they hit (20 bullet damage = 1 % condition; wheels much more). Off = the game's own rule.
A wheel shot or slashed to 0 condition jumps off its car.
Pistols/revolvers: damage falls off linearly with distance - half at 50 % of this range, the bullet is gone at 100 %. Metres.
SMGs, falloff range in metres (half damage at half range).
Automatic rifles and machine guns, falloff range in metres.
Sniper/scoped rifles, falloff range in metres.
Shotguns, falloff range in metres.
Crossbows, falloff range in metres.
Combat HUD: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
Weapon crosshair: 0 = none, 1 = vanilla, 2 = two horizontal lines, 3 = dot. Follows the game's weapon and aiming visibility.
Show the game's selection dot without a weapon. Independent of the weapon crosshair.
Damage numbers, hit marker and headshot sound for your hits (master switch for HitMarker, FloatingDamage and HeadshotSound). The crosshair settings are independent.
A diagonal cross flashes at the screen centre when your bullet hits a creature (white, red for a headshot).

Damage your hits do, shown as: 0 = nothing, 1 = a list in the top right corner, 2 = numbers floating up from the hit point. White = damage, red with '!' = headshot, light blue = % of condition taken off a vehicle part.
Play a sound for your headshots. Near-simultaneous hits are coalesced and overlap is limited without restarting sounds.
Volume of the headshot sound, percent.
Third person: orbit the camera around the character (held, or press on / press off with ToggleObserving). None = no key.
Optional separate climb key (the game's Jump key also climbs with JumpTriggersClimbing). None = no key.
Driving: start / stop the cassette player. Starting at zero volume sets 0.5. None = no hotkey.
Driving: cassette volume -0.1 (also keypad minus). None = no hotkey.
Driving: cassette volume +0.1 (+ on the main keyboard, also keypad plus). None = no hotkey.
Debug: spawn a Gungirl six metres ahead.

Your shout (with 'Shout modifier' held): you yell like a raider and every NPC hostile to you within 25 m comes to check. None = off. (Alt+Q is shared on purpose with the Patrols merchant stop signal.)
Hold this and press 'Shout' to shout (either Alt works when this is an Alt key); the game's own Q actions are ignored while it is held. None = the key alone.
Guns: key polled for hold-to-unload only if the game's Reload input axis cannot be read (normally the game's own Reload binding is used).
Patrols: open the patrol / convoy / merchant / loot editor (also F7 > Patrols & vehicles > Patrol editor). None = unbound
Patrols: save the vehicle you sit in as a template (only while seated; also F7 > Template recorder). None = unbound
Patrols: toggle the bus passenger pose editor (also F7 > Seat & turret poses). None = unbound
Patrols: toggle the merchant item placement editor (also F7 > Merchants). None = unbound
Key that shows or hides the quest log.
Press to send your hired help away at any time. None = off (you can still dismiss them by talking to them).
Talk to the friendly NPC under your aim. Apocatalker owns its own interaction when installed.
Your multiplayer display name (1-48 characters). Empty uses the Steam or launcher name. Change before hosting or joining.
Show floating multiplayer names facing your rendered camera. This is your own HUD preference.
NPC AI & navigation: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
NPCs see (field of view, light, flashlight), hear gunshots, shouts, engines and explosions, remember where you were and search. Off = the game's own sensors.
NPCs steer around obstacles, use the maps of camps, caves and buildings, take shooting positions, kneel and aim. Off = the game's own movement.
NPC gunmen pace their bursts: they hold fire beyond their gun's reach, take longer to aim at a distance and lead moving targets.
Camp raiders who lose you go back to their spawn spot, and walk a short round in their camp while nothing happens.
The idle behaviour also for the peaceful Coyote towns.
NPCs of the same faction walk through each other while they fight, search or walk home - no bumping, no blocking a passage. Solid again once they are idle.
Sandstorms (and ApocaDustStorm's dust storms) dim NPC sight and hearing; tornado funnels make NPCs forget what they were doing. Off = storms do not affect the senses.

Scorpions burrow into sand when nothing alerts them (and come up every 10-30 s), eyes above the surface. Big scorpions also hunt underground: they travel under the sand and come up behind their enemy.
Scorpions wait until a target comes within 3-5 m. Spiders wait in darkness, but react to shouts, gunfire, light and a nest's web being touched.
Small spiders zigzag in when they get close to you over open ground, leap at you from 5-6 m, bite and run off before trying again.
Caves, wrecks and camps with spiders become spider nests: webs across their openings and on the ground, big spiders sitting in the webs. Touch a web and the whole nest comes at you.
Quadrupeds commit to dodgeable running bites and use faster bites at close range. Without the animation bundle, the original procedural bite is used.
Retargeted animations on hounds, Grimhound and nightwalkers. Requires NPC/Models/npcai_dogs.bundle; otherwise the existing procedural bite remains active.
Non-boss quadrupeds alternate standing and lying idle, spending a random 10-25 seconds in each pose. Threats interrupt rest through get-up.
Optional short, collision-checked jumping bite. Native damage is applied only if the target remains within reach at contact.
With FlyingKlick's Dog Companion installed: the companion dog uses the same dog animations (locomotion, bites, sitting in vehicles, sneaking). Off = Dog Companion's own behaviour.
Width of an NPC's field of view, degrees.
How far an NPC sees in daylight, m (and at any light if your flashlight is on).
How far an NPC sees in full darkness, m.
Gungirl model, relative to the NPC asset folder. Restart to reload.
Gungirl texture, relative to the NPC asset folder. Restart to reload.
Comma-separated attachment name prefixes hidden on newly dressed Gungirls.
Female voice folder, relative to the NPC asset folder. WAV and OGG; OGG wins. Restart to reload.
Match female voice loudness to the native clips.
Female voice volume multiplier.
Shortest combat shout pause for newly dressed females, seconds.
Longest combat shout pause for newly dressed females, seconds.
With many NPCs around, each one thinks less often (saves CPU in big fights).
Shoota model, relative to the NPC asset folder. Restart to reload.
Shoota texture, relative to the NPC asset folder. Restart to reload.
Comma-separated attachment name prefixes hidden on newly dressed Shootas.
Convert a share of newly spawned Flexa and Sprokka raiders to Gungirl and Shoota. Existing females keep their identity when off.
Percentage of eligible new raiders and crew converted to female variants.
Apply the female population chance to new Flexa/Sprokka drivers, passengers and turret gunners. Explicit female template choices still apply when off.
Patrols, traffic & War Rig: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
Raider patrols and convoys spawn on their own while you play. Off = no automatic spawns at all (the editor's test spawns still work)
World traffic: Scrapyard and Coyote groups that meet fight each other (resolved off-screen when you are far away; wrecks, corpses and a skull on the debug map). Off = no new battles
World traffic: Coyote trader buses (General / Mechanic / Organic shops) travel and park; stop one with Alt+Q or the horn. Off = no automatic merchant routes (same as Max merchants 0)
A template's human turrets fight: a Warboy crouching on the roof throws blast lances (and may leap at you: "Witness me!"), a gunner shoots all around with its own gun. Off = they just ride along

Ranged humans (Boltjaw/Flexa/Lugnut/Scrud/Sprokka) in a car use their vanilla targeting and ranged attack: the passenger whenever a target is in the fire arc, the driver in bursts. Off = everybody just rides along
An AI car that hits you (on foot or in your car) hurts you. The game's own bumper damage only works against creatures, not the player
Ram damage also while you sit in your own car (the game's own CrashDamage still applies by your speed). Off = only on foot

A raider car built from a template that has a cassette in its radio plays it at full volume from the moment it spawns, until you switch the radio off. Off = the cassette sits in the radio, silent, as in a parked car

Raider cars wear the paint jobs from the Patrols\Textures folder (body textures, truck container sides and inside). Off = they keep the game's own textures (cars spawned from then on; the textures are not loaded at game start)
Override template explodeChance with 100%. Requires a dead driver and all living passengers/turrets to leave. An alive driver bailout never explodes the car; captured cars are protected
Remove raider cars you left behind. A car you have ever sat in is never removed (the game itself only deletes cars beyond 5 km)
Raider engines overheat like yours (smoke, steam, the engine wears down). Off = they never overheat while their crew drives; a car you take or an engine you loot heats normally again
Every patrol and convoy group can spawn from the start: their minimum distance travelled and minimum boss kills are ignored. Off = groups unlock with distance and bosses as set in the editor
NPC module: no crew AI while seated; dismounted bandits fight using baked-map navigation; they hunt you only once they have seen or fought you, and keep track of you for a while after a fight
World traffic: groups of 2-5 raiders walk between camps over open land (simulated while you are far away). Crew left without a usable car also walk to a nearby camp. Off = no new foot patrols

Debug: dismounted crew whose fight is over walk back to their car and take their seats again (a passenger or gunner takes the wheel if the driver is dead); the car leaves once every living member is aboard
World traffic: varied attack runs and vehicle-checked camp approaches
Allow the abandoned War Rig POI and manual War Rig spawns. World discovery chance is in POI / World. Existing rigs are unaffected
Rescue a War Rig (with its truck and passengers) after a confirmed fall below the terrain. Off by default
Lowest condition (%) of a spawned raider car's parts that have one (engine, radiator, wheels ...)
Highest condition (%) of a spawned raider car's parts; the roll is weighted toward two thirds of the way from Min to Max
% chance for each part of an exploded raider car to keep its condition (MinPartHealth..MaxPartHealth) instead of dropping at 0 %. 20 = about one part in five, 0 = all junk, 100 = all usable
Damage multiplier when any car hits a creature other than the player, including NPC-driven cars: 4 = four times the game's bumper damage, 1 = vanilla, 0 = no damage
Occupants only shoot at a target closer than this, m
% chance that an unhurt blast-lance rider screams "Witness me!" and leaps at your car when you drive close (a wounded rider always does). 100 = every time
Maximum merchants, with at most one of each shop type. Zero disables automatic merchants.
Average percentage of Max merchants represented by routes. Whole slots are guaranteed; the remaining fractional slot is rolled at each check. 100 fills the cap; zero creates no merchant routes.

Check and adjust merchant route population this often, including replacing departed merchants. No immediate replacement when a route ends. Loaded merchants finish their visit before excess routes are removed.
Size of every patrol / convoy that spawns, for weaker PCs: below 100 the group loses cars at random down to this share (rounded down, never below one car; a convoy keeps all of its trucks)
Maximum tracked patrol groups, including arrived and passing Coyote groups; replaces density
Maximum tracked convoy groups, including arrived groups; replaces density
Limit physical encounter cars; pending builds count toward the same budget
Maximum cars in one patrol or convoy; cargo trucks have priority
Combined physical car budget when encounters overlap near the player
Simulated/cruising patrol speed
Simulated/cruising convoy speed
Loaded, uncleared raider camps support base patrols and convoys; incoming Coyote patrols do not require camps
Performance & optimization: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
Player body & animation: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.

Your character's body. Male, Female, Merchant, Bodyguard, Sprokka, OrganicMechanic, Gungirl and Shoota use Wild Wasteland player animations, online or offline. Legacy Pistoleer/Mechanic choices map to Bodyguard/Merchant.
The game's Change Camera key switches to a camera behind your character, on foot and in cars (replaces the game's own car camera).

Third person, observing key ([Keys] Observe). Off: hold the key to orbit the camera around the character; it returns behind the character when you let go. On: a press starts observing and the camera stays where you left it until the next press.

Third person with a weapon drawn: the crosshair sits where your shots and melee hits really land (the eye ray from the head). Without a weapon, or Off: the crosshair stays centred and the camera turns toward the aim point.
First person: see the body (legs and torso when you look down, the shadow, the body in the driver's seat). Off = only the first-person arms.
Full Body: show the first-person body only on foot, keeping the driver's first-person view clear.
First person with nothing in hand: show the body's own arms (idle/walk swing, hands on the wheel in a car). Off = no body arms in first person; the game's weapon and item arms always show.
First Person Arms: show the empty-handed arms only on foot, hiding the hands on the wheel while driving.
The game's first-person arms and kick leg wear your character's skin (Female; Male keeps the game's own).
Your character replaces the game's man in the driver's seat (posed from the seat, guns and throws from the seat) and on the TAB screen picture.
Show the carried equipment on the body: backpack, long guns on the back, sidearms, blades, binoculars, flashlight (with its glow).
Female character: four female hurt sounds and a female death sound.
First person: frame-rate independent weapon / item sway (the game's own sway stutters with uneven frame times).
First person: the gun eases between hip and sights (right mouse button) instead of jumping. Time in F7.
Third person on foot: an item, part or switch close to the crosshair on screen is picked even if the eye ray misses it.

Third person: keep the camera distance and make geometry between camera and body semi-transparent (prototype; roofs and vehicles get a larger window; not inside caves). Off = the camera moves in front of obstacles.
Third person while driving: also use the camera culling (needs CameraCulling on).
Climb onto reachable solid ledges on foot.
The game's Jump key climbs onto a reachable ledge or catches one within arm's reach during a jump. Otherwise it jumps normally.
Show ignition off, handbrake engaged and playing cassette with volume in the top right while driving.
Show the vehicle hotkeys on the left while driving. Hiding the hints keeps the keys working.
Adds an "Ignition" row to the game's Controls screen (default E): each press performs one ignition/start panel click (ignition on, crank, then stop on standard cars).
A blast lance thrown from the driver's seat flies out of your own car instead of blowing up on it.
Points of interest: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
Chance for each added POI in each generated 5 km terrain slice. 100 guarantees one site per slice for debugging. Changes affect newly generated slices.
Quests & hiring: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
How many quests you can carry at once.
Multiplies every reward (hand-written and generated).
Show a short list of your active quests in the top-right corner.
NPCs can offer randomly generated jobs as well as the ones in quests.txt.
Which kinds of random jobs may be generated (fetch, kill, goto, talk, clear, takeover, deliver). Add takeover or deliver here if your config was made by an older version.
Bodyguards, pups, bolters, pistoleers, gunnars and luggers can be hired for reputation (needs the NPCAI and Apocapatrol mods).
The follower rides in your car's passenger seat when it is free, and gets out when you do.
A follower with a ranged weapon shoots at your enemies from the passenger seat, the way Apocapatrol's crews do (needs Apocapatrol).
Fetch quests also count items in your hand and quick slots.
Merchants (see Npcs) buy and sell reputation with their own faction in the talk window: Buy / Sell 1, 5, 25, 50 or as many as possible.
Play recorded voice lines for quests that have them (Voice Actors\<actor>\<quest id>\offer.wav, accept.wav, remind.wav, done.wav).
Volume of the voice lines, 0 to 10. Every recording is first levelled to the same loudness; 5 is full level, above 5 boosts it further.
Where the Voice Actors folder is. Empty = a 'Voice Actors' folder next to the plugin DLL (or one level above it).
Survival: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
Remove only selected, positively identified disposable objects after a verified save. Unknown ownership/references always retain objects.
Remove abandoned Zombie_Runner_Dead roots only; never resource carcasses, live actors or player bodies.
Remove empty ammo/battery packs only when they have no remaining sale value and have never been observed in player custody.
Must remain this far from every connected player.
Continuous active gameplay beyond the minimum distance. Enabling cleanup starts a fresh observation period.
Create separate autosaves for offline or hosted worlds. Manual saves are never replaced by autosaving.
Real minutes between autosaves.
Visible server-wide autosave countdown. At least 30 seconds, with notices at 30 and 15 seconds and a final warning before saving.
Allow autosaves while the offline player, host or guests are driving or riding in any vehicle. Manual and exit saves are always available in vehicles.
Number of separate autosaves per world lineage. Manual saves are not pruned.
Verified previous versions per save. Interrupted recovery and deleted-save backups are always retained.
Capture a gameplay thumbnail for each save.
Weather: master switch for this whole feature group. Turning it off at runtime stops it immediately (patches removed); turning it on starts it again.
Color of the incoming front and its cloud bank. Live RGB controls are in Developer > Weather > Weather visual preview.
Interior haze and sky/lighting tint. Applies live; does not recolor UI or the independent vanilla sand effect.
Independent color of the dense rotating hurricane shell. Does not fill its central eye.
Independent tint of the game's local sand/cloud particles, with live RGB controls.
Show moving Weather storm areas on the map. Critical storms lift vehicles and damage actors in hurricane sand walls; eyes are safe.
Extra world dimming with depth inside a storm. 0 = none; 1 = complete darkness in the deep interior. HUD stays readable.
Columns per square kilometre of critical storm area, rounded to the nearest whole column. Zero disables columns. Applies live and does not change with Performance presets.
Width of the broad leading sand front. Applies live to preview regions and their map areas.
Depth behind the front; sand fades and the footprint narrows toward the rear. Applies live.
Sliced background work (bakes, scans) stops for the frame once Wild Wasteland used this much time.
Seconds to wait for an unload animation phase before completing it.
Your own guns follow the same rules: visible bullets with travel time, the same range falloff and vehicle-part hits.
Every gun (NPC and yours) does full damage until this % of its range, then the damage falls off to 0 at the range. 0 = falloff from the muzzle (half damage at 50 %).
Thickness of NPC bullets, m, added to the target's hitbox (your body/head shapes, other targets' colliders). 0 = hairline. Your own bullets are always a hairline.
Damage multiplier for NPC shotgun pellets (the game's shotgunners do 5-8 per ray x 4 rays per blast, a third of a rifle burst).
Pellets per vanilla shotgun ray (a vanilla blast is 4 rays; 3 = 12 pellets). The blast's damage is split between them.
Extra spread of each pellet, degrees.
Player shotgun pellet distribution, %: 0 favours the rim, 50 is uniform across the circle, 100 favours the centre. Full spread remains possible; applies to the next shot.
NPC shotgun pellet distribution, %: 0 favours the rim, 50 is uniform across the circle, 100 favours the centre. Applies to extra pellet spread; NPC aim and lead are separate.
Your body as NPC bullets see it: a capsule from your feet to your neck with this radius, m (the game's own collider is only 0.17-0.20).
Your head as NPC bullets see it: a sphere of this radius at the top of your body, m.
Bullet damage that takes 1 % off a vehicle part condition.
Wheels (and tyres) lose this many times more condition per bullet - and per blow of your melee weapons - than other vehicle parts, so shooting or slashing the wheels is the way to stop a car.
Melee weapons (name contains one of these) that use StabSound when hitting living actors or corpses instead of the game's knife hit. Every melee hit on a corpse shows blood.
The stab sound for blades on living actors and corpses (WAV, relative to BepInEx\plugins\WildWasteland\Guns\; the old Gunplay plugin folder is used as a fallback). Missing file: the game's knife hit.
NPCs aim at the centre of your body. Off = the game's own aim point, your head, which with the game's aim jitter sends many shots over your head. (Also needs F6 [Guns] NpcAim.)
NPCs aim where a moving target will be when the bullet arrives (the game's hitscan never had to). Changing direction still beats them. (Also needs F6 [Guns] NpcAim.)
How much of the ideal lead NPCs apply: 1 = perfect prediction, 0 = none. Each NPC rolls a personal skill between half of this and all of it.
Random error on the NPC's estimate of your speed, +/- %, per shot.
Longest flight time NPCs lead for, s (bolts at long range).
Bullet tracer colour (RGBA hex). Unlit: same brightness day and night.
Brightness multiplier of tracers and bolts.
Tracer line length, m.
Tracer line width, m.
Crossbow bolt colour (RGBA hex).
Bolt line length, m.
Bolt line width, m.
Most bullets in flight at once; shots above this hit instantly (vanilla style) instead.
NPC bullets that hit the world show the same impact (sparks, sound) your own hits do; the game showed nothing for their misses.
Extra sparks, smoke and a bullet mark on anything that is part of a car - attached parts, the body and frame, loose parts - except wheels (any bullet), using the game's MetalImpact effect.
Size of the metal sparks effect (1 = the prefab's own, demo-scene size).
Size of the dot crosshair (style 3) relative to the vanilla crosshair.
While the game's Canvas/MousePoint and MouseCrosshair are not found (menus, loading), look for them at most this often, s.
Sample gain applied once when headshot.mp3 is decoded (AudioSource volume cannot exceed 1). Applies on the next load (module off/on).
Headshots closer together than this play one sound, s.
Font size of the damage list, px; floating numbers use +4.
Hit marker size, px.
Lifetime of a floating damage number, s.
Lifetime of a line in the top-right damage list, s.
Maximum lines in the top-right damage list.
How long the hit marker shows, s.
Hits on the same target within this time are merged into one number (shotgun pellets), s.
Creatures that lie in wait (exact prefab names).
They let a target come this close at the least before attacking, m (chosen at random each time they settle).
... and at the most, m.
Idle quadrupeds stand or lie at least this long before switching, s.
... and at the most, s.

Lying quadrupeds: the front half (chest, front legs, head) is tilted up at the waist until the shoulders stand as high over the hips as they do standing. This adds to (or, negative, takes from) that height, m.

How quickly NPCs think and react, as % of the default: every wait of the brain (looks, backing out of a stuck, resting, keeping a way around an obstacle, rechecks while holding) is scaled by this. 50 = twice as quick, 500 = five times slower.
How fast an NPC turns its body, degrees per second - also to face you for a shot (the game snapped instantly).
A gunman holding a shooting position keeps the gun up and aimed at you between bursts (the game lowered it to the idle pose and raised it only for the shot).
% chance that a gunman kneels when he takes a shooting position (humans only; he stands up when he moves again). He is harder to hit kneeling: his hitbox shrinks with him.
How far ahead a moving NPC looks for obstacles, m.
How far ahead a melee NPC looks, m (they turn quicker than a gunman needs).
Half-angle of the feeler fan around the direction to the target, degrees.
Feeler rays per look (odd; fewer = cheaper, coarser).
A moving NPC also checks for ground 1.5 m along its chosen direction and picks another when there is a drop (one extra ray).
A gunman holding a shooting position rolls this % at every hold recheck (1-4 s) to run toward you for AdvanceMin..AdvanceMax s instead.
Shortest advance, s.
Longest advance, s.
A stuck NPC backs up this long, s, before trying another way.

CT1 Sliced item culling. The game's 5/10-second item culling and cleanup sweeps run a few entries per frame instead of the whole list in one frame (same rules).
CT3 Event-driven vehicle hinges. Vehicle hinge FSMs that check every frame whether a part is attached sleep until the part count actually changes (exact).
CT4 Direct NWH access for car FSMs. Pedal, RPM/gear and handbrake FSMs read and write the vehicle physics directly instead of by reflection (exact).
CT5 Sleeping wait-until polls. Item, vehicle and NPC FSMs that only wait for a value to change sleep until it does (exact).
CT6 Light flicker manager. Flickering camp lights update at a fixed rate and only near the camera instead of every frame everywhere.
CT7 Player sheet texts and day clock. Hidden player-sheet ammo/armor texts refresh twice a second while the sheet is closed; the day clock runs at its intended 0.2 s instead of every frame.
CT8 Coyote faction broadcast. Repeated hits on Coyotes no longer re-broadcast the hostility event to every FSM in the game, only to those still friendly.
CT9 No duplicate Rigidbody adds. Car parts no longer try to add a second Rigidbody on every spawn (same result, no error spam).
CT9 No restart for empty data FSMs. Item data FSMs (one empty state) are not restarted every time an item is re-activated (exact).
CT11 Sleeping option toggles. Settings-menu toggles stop checking their value every frame while it does not change (exact).
CT10 Player collider height writes. The player's collider height is written only when it changes (crouch/stand), not twice every frame (exact).

PM2 Fast targeted events. Events sent to an object no longer search every FSM in the game (stalls on POI entry, save and load). Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).
PM3 Fast FSM disable/destroy. Disabling or destroying an FSM searched the whole list of enabled FSMs (slow Unity comparisons). Same result, found by reference.
PM4 Broadcast without list copies. Game-wide events (Save/Load settings, day change, faction changes) reuse one buffer instead of copying every FSM.

PM5 PlayMaker GUI loop and visibility events. PlayMaker's GUI pass visits only the few FSMs that draw anything, unused OnGUI helpers stop running, and unhandled became-visible events are skipped. Same result.
PM6 Skip unhandled trigger/collision events. Trigger and collision callbacks no longer push an event nobody listens to through the whole FSM event path. Same result.

PM7 One camera pick raycast per frame. The ~40 cursor raycasts the game's FSMs make every frame (one per layer mask) share one raycast. Same hits. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

PM10 Reuse unchanged number strings. HUD FSMs format the same number into a new string every frame; the previous string is reused while the number is unchanged. Same text, less garbage. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

FS1 Idle FSMs skip their update. FSMs waiting for an event (doors, items, switches, parked cars) stop running their per-frame update until something happens to them. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

FS2 Compiled Get/Set Property. Get/Set Property actions (vehicle input, wheels, rigidbodies) use compiled accessors instead of reflection. Same values, no garbage. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).
FS3 Compiled Call Method actions. Call Method actions call the target method through a compiled delegate instead of reflection. Same calls, same results.
FS4 Faster FSM loading on spawn. Spawning objects with FSMs (vehicles, items, camps) creates their actions with compiled constructors and field setters instead of reflection. Same values.

PERFORMANCE (Low), BALANCED, VISUALS (Max), VANILLA (default). Vanilla preserves original visuals, simulation settings and item cleanup; exact optimizations (no visible change) are not affected. Saved Low/Max values remain compatible.

EN1 Point-light shadows, budget and distance culling. Point lights lose their cube shadows except the nearest few; far point lights are switched off; headlights reach less far; fewer per-pixel lights.

EN2 Skip zero-intensity screen-space shadows, lean Sharpen. Exact: no visible change. Skips the PPU screen-space-shadow effect while its intensity is 0 and renders Sharpen without its unused render texture.
EN2 Replace the no-op TAA with SMAA / FXAA. The game's TAA has zero blending (costs time, smooths nothing). Performance uses FXAA, Balanced/Visuals SMAA.
EN3 Sun shadow distance, cascades, resolution, layer culling. Shorter, cheaper sun shadows; small items, food, weapons and NPCs stop casting sun shadows a few dozen metres away.
EN4 Terrain pixel error, base map and grass distance. Coarser far terrain mesh, earlier low-res base map, grass drawn less far and slightly thinner.
EN5 Particle prewarm, off-screen culling, collision, lights. Fires and smoke no longer pre-simulate when a camp spawns, pause off-screen, collide cheaper and drop their particle lights.
RC1 No shadows from tiny objects. Objects smaller than a few centimetres to decimetres (cans, bolts, small props) stop casting shadows.
RC2 Cull-only LOD groups and LOD bias. Props and buildings without LODs stop rendering when they are only a few pixels tall; LOD bias follows the preset.
RC3 Per-layer view distances. Car parts stop rendering beyond 300 m, NPCs beyond 600 m, cars beyond 2.5 km. Items, food and weapons retain their original camera distances.
RC4 Shorter far clip plane (Performance). Performance preset: the view ends at 6 km instead of 10 km.
RC8 Texture resolution and anisotropic filtering (Low). Performance preset: half-resolution textures and non-forced anisotropic filtering (saves video memory).

RC5 Terrain streaming budget. Fewer, lower-priority terrain generation threads and fewer objects placed per frame when a tile appears (smaller hitches, objects pop in a little later).
RC7 Resting items use cheaper CCD. Loose items lying still use speculative continuous collision; fast-moving ones keep full continuous collision.
EN6 Physics step cap and sleep threshold. Caps physics catch-up after a slow frame (the game slows down instead of stalling) and lets resting bodies sleep from the start.
RC6 Off-screen NPC animation and IK. NPC skeletons stop updating while off-screen; leg/arm IK of NPCs runs only when visible and near.

EN8 Incremental GC time slice. Shorter incremental garbage-collection slices per frame (smoother frame times while the GC runs).

CT1 Sliced item culling. The game's 5/10-second item culling and cleanup sweeps run a few entries per frame instead of the whole list in one frame (same rules).
CT3 Event-driven vehicle hinges. Vehicle hinge FSMs that check every frame whether a part is attached sleep until the part count actually changes (exact).
CT4 Direct NWH access for car FSMs. Pedal, RPM/gear and handbrake FSMs read and write the vehicle physics directly instead of by reflection (exact).
CT5 Sleeping wait-until polls. Item, vehicle and NPC FSMs that only wait for a value to change sleep until it does (exact).
CT6 Light flicker manager. Flickering camp lights update at a fixed rate and only near the camera instead of every frame everywhere.
CT7 Player sheet texts and day clock. Hidden player-sheet ammo/armor texts refresh twice a second while the sheet is closed; the day clock runs at its intended 0.2 s instead of every frame.
CT8 Coyote faction broadcast. Repeated hits on Coyotes no longer re-broadcast the hostility event to every FSM in the game, only to those still friendly.
CT9 No duplicate Rigidbody adds. Car parts no longer try to add a second Rigidbody on every spawn (same result, no error spam).
CT9 No restart for empty data FSMs. Item data FSMs (one empty state) are not restarted every time an item is re-activated (exact).
CT11 Sleeping option toggles. Settings-menu toggles stop checking their value every frame while it does not change (exact).
CT10 Player collider height writes. The player's collider height is written only when it changes (crouch/stand), not twice every frame (exact).

PM2 Fast targeted events. Events sent to an object no longer search every FSM in the game (stalls on POI entry, save and load). Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).
PM3 Fast FSM disable/destroy. Disabling or destroying an FSM searched the whole list of enabled FSMs (slow Unity comparisons). Same result, found by reference.
PM4 Broadcast without list copies. Game-wide events (Save/Load settings, day change, faction changes) reuse one buffer instead of copying every FSM.

PM5 PlayMaker GUI loop and visibility events. PlayMaker's GUI pass visits only the few FSMs that draw anything, unused OnGUI helpers stop running, and unhandled became-visible events are skipped. Same result.
PM6 Skip unhandled trigger/collision events. Trigger and collision callbacks no longer push an event nobody listens to through the whole FSM event path. Same result.

PM7 One camera pick raycast per frame. The ~40 cursor raycasts the game's FSMs make every frame (one per layer mask) share one raycast. Same hits. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

PM10 Reuse unchanged number strings. HUD FSMs format the same number into a new string every frame; the previous string is reused while the number is unchanged. Same text, less garbage. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

FS1 Idle FSMs skip their update. FSMs waiting for an event (doors, items, switches, parked cars) stop running their per-frame update until something happens to them. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

FS2 Compiled Get/Set Property. Get/Set Property actions (vehicle input, wheels, rigidbodies) use compiled accessors instead of reflection. Same values, no garbage. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).
FS3 Compiled Call Method actions. Call Method actions call the target method through a compiled delegate instead of reflection. Same calls, same results.
FS4 Faster FSM loading on spawn. Spawning objects with FSMs (vehicles, items, camps) creates their actions with compiled constructors and field setters instead of reflection. Same values.

PERFORMANCE (Low), BALANCED, VISUALS (Max), VANILLA (default). Vanilla preserves original visuals, simulation settings and item cleanup; exact optimizations (no visible change) are not affected. Saved Low/Max values remain compatible.

EN1 Point-light shadows, budget and distance culling. Point lights lose their cube shadows except the nearest few; far point lights are switched off; headlights reach less far; fewer per-pixel lights.

EN2 Skip zero-intensity screen-space shadows, lean Sharpen. Exact: no visible change. Skips the PPU screen-space-shadow effect while its intensity is 0 and renders Sharpen without its unused render texture.
EN2 Replace the no-op TAA with SMAA / FXAA. The game's TAA has zero blending (costs time, smooths nothing). Performance uses FXAA, Balanced/Visuals SMAA.
EN3 Sun shadow distance, cascades, resolution, layer culling. Shorter, cheaper sun shadows; small items, food, weapons and NPCs stop casting sun shadows a few dozen metres away.
EN4 Terrain pixel error, base map and grass distance. Coarser far terrain mesh, earlier low-res base map, grass drawn less far and slightly thinner.
EN5 Particle prewarm, off-screen culling, collision, lights. Fires and smoke no longer pre-simulate when a camp spawns, pause off-screen, collide cheaper and drop their particle lights.
RC1 No shadows from tiny objects. Objects smaller than a few centimetres to decimetres (cans, bolts, small props) stop casting shadows.
RC2 Cull-only LOD groups and LOD bias. Props and buildings without LODs stop rendering when they are only a few pixels tall; LOD bias follows the preset.
RC3 Per-layer view distances. Car parts stop rendering beyond 300 m, NPCs beyond 600 m, cars beyond 2.5 km. Items, food and weapons retain their original camera distances.
RC4 Shorter far clip plane (Performance). Performance preset: the view ends at 6 km instead of 10 km.
RC8 Texture resolution and anisotropic filtering (Low). Performance preset: half-resolution textures and non-forced anisotropic filtering (saves video memory).

CT1 Sliced item culling. The game's 5/10-second item culling and cleanup sweeps run a few entries per frame instead of the whole list in one frame (same rules).
CT3 Event-driven vehicle hinges. Vehicle hinge FSMs that check every frame whether a part is attached sleep until the part count actually changes (exact).
CT4 Direct NWH access for car FSMs. Pedal, RPM/gear and handbrake FSMs read and write the vehicle physics directly instead of by reflection (exact).
CT5 Sleeping wait-until polls. Item, vehicle and NPC FSMs that only wait for a value to change sleep until it does (exact).
CT6 Light flicker manager. Flickering camp lights update at a fixed rate and only near the camera instead of every frame everywhere.
CT7 Player sheet texts and day clock. Hidden player-sheet ammo/armor texts refresh twice a second while the sheet is closed; the day clock runs at its intended 0.2 s instead of every frame.
CT8 Coyote faction broadcast. Repeated hits on Coyotes no longer re-broadcast the hostility event to every FSM in the game, only to those still friendly.
CT9 No duplicate Rigidbody adds. Car parts no longer try to add a second Rigidbody on every spawn (same result, no error spam).
CT9 No restart for empty data FSMs. Item data FSMs (one empty state) are not restarted every time an item is re-activated (exact).
CT11 Sleeping option toggles. Settings-menu toggles stop checking their value every frame while it does not change (exact).
CT10 Player collider height writes. The player's collider height is written only when it changes (crouch/stand), not twice every frame (exact).

PM2 Fast targeted events. Events sent to an object no longer search every FSM in the game (stalls on POI entry, save and load). Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).
PM3 Fast FSM disable/destroy. Disabling or destroying an FSM searched the whole list of enabled FSMs (slow Unity comparisons). Same result, found by reference.
PM4 Broadcast without list copies. Game-wide events (Save/Load settings, day change, faction changes) reuse one buffer instead of copying every FSM.

PM5 PlayMaker GUI loop and visibility events. PlayMaker's GUI pass visits only the few FSMs that draw anything, unused OnGUI helpers stop running, and unhandled became-visible events are skipped. Same result.
PM6 Skip unhandled trigger/collision events. Trigger and collision callbacks no longer push an event nobody listens to through the whole FSM event path. Same result.

PM7 One camera pick raycast per frame. The ~40 cursor raycasts the game's FSMs make every frame (one per layer mask) share one raycast. Same hits. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

PM10 Reuse unchanged number strings. HUD FSMs format the same number into a new string every frame; the previous string is reused while the number is unchanged. Same text, less garbage. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

FS1 Idle FSMs skip their update. FSMs waiting for an event (doors, items, switches, parked cars) stop running their per-frame update until something happens to them. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).

FS2 Compiled Get/Set Property. Get/Set Property actions (vehicle input, wheels, rigidbodies) use compiled accessors instead of reflection. Same values, no garbage. Shadow = vanilla runs, the optimized result is only compared (mismatches shown in Developer).
FS3 Compiled Call Method actions. Call Method actions call the target method through a compiled delegate instead of reflection. Same calls, same results.
FS4 Faster FSM loading on spawn. Spawning objects with FSMs (vehicles, items, camps) creates their actions with compiled constructors and field setters instead of reflection. Same values.

PERFORMANCE (Low), BALANCED, VISUALS (Max), VANILLA (default). Vanilla preserves original visuals, simulation settings and item cleanup; exact optimizations (no visible change) are not affected. Saved Low/Max values remain compatible.

EN1 Point-light shadows, budget and distance culling. Point lights lose their cube shadows except the nearest few; far point lights are switched off; headlights reach less far; fewer per-pixel lights.

EN2 Skip zero-intensity screen-space shadows, lean Sharpen. Exact: no visible change. Skips the PPU screen-space-shadow effect while its intensity is 0 and renders Sharpen without its unused render texture.
EN2 Replace the no-op TAA with SMAA / FXAA. The game's TAA has zero blending (costs time, smooths nothing). Performance uses FXAA, Balanced/Visuals SMAA.
EN3 Sun shadow distance, cascades, resolution, layer culling. Shorter, cheaper sun shadows; small items, food, weapons and NPCs stop casting sun shadows a few dozen metres away.
EN4 Terrain pixel error, base map and grass distance. Coarser far terrain mesh, earlier low-res base map, grass drawn less far and slightly thinner.
EN5 Particle prewarm, off-screen culling, collision, lights. Fires and smoke no longer pre-simulate when a camp spawns, pause off-screen, collide cheaper and drop their particle lights.
RC1 No shadows from tiny objects. Objects smaller than a few centimetres to decimetres (cans, bolts, small props) stop casting shadows.
RC2 Cull-only LOD groups and LOD bias. Props and buildings without LODs stop rendering when they are only a few pixels tall; LOD bias follows the preset.
RC3 Per-layer view distances. Car parts stop rendering beyond 300 m, NPCs beyond 600 m, cars beyond 2.5 km. Items, food and weapons retain their original camera distances.
RC4 Shorter far clip plane (Performance). Performance preset: the view ends at 6 km instead of 10 km.
RC8 Texture resolution and anisotropic filtering (Low). Performance preset: half-resolution textures and non-forced anisotropic filtering (saves video memory).

CT2 Parked car simulation LOD. Cars nobody uses stop running their dashboard/pedal FSMs when far away and their wheel physics while frozen.
RC5 Terrain streaming budget. Fewer, lower-priority terrain generation threads and fewer objects placed per frame when a tile appears (smaller hitches, objects pop in a little later).
RC7 Resting items use cheaper CCD. Loose items lying still use speculative continuous collision; fast-moving ones keep full continuous collision.
EN6 Physics step cap and sleep threshold. Caps physics catch-up after a slow frame (the game slows down instead of stalling) and lets resting bodies sleep from the start.
RC6 Off-screen NPC animation and IK. NPC skeletons stop updating while off-screen; leg/arm IK of NPCs runs only when visible and near.
EN6 Floating-origin jump body scan. Floating-origin jumps scan the scene's rigidbodies once instead of twice (exact).

EN7 Sky weather evaluation rate. Sky/fog weather curves are re-evaluated a few times per second instead of on every physics step (every frame during weather changes).
EN8 Incremental GC time slice. Shorter incremental garbage-collection slices per frame (smoother frame times while the GC runs).

For quest writers: log every NPC you talk to and keep lists of their names and home camps in npc_names.txt and npc_locations.txt next to the DLL.
Deliveries go to a friendly camp at least this far (m) from the giver.
Deliveries go to a friendly camp at most this far (m) from the giver.
Time limit of a delivery: this many IN-GAME hours (the game clock, not real time)...
...plus this many in-game hours per km to the camp (straight line). Pausing stops it; sleeping uses it up.
Talk to someone friendly within this many metres of the camp to hand the goods over.
A person without a faction tag counts as living at the nearest camp / building / cave within this many metres, and takes that place's faction.
Unity tags the game uses for human factions (taken from NPCAI). NPCs with one of these tags belong to that faction; camps with an EnemySpawn_<Faction> child belong to it too.
Names that count as people (not animals) when working out who lives where. Enemies with these names are protected from kill quests of their own faction.
Generated go-to quests pick points of interest at least this far from the giver.
Generated go-to quests pick points of interest at most this far from the giver.
Who can be hired and for how much reputation (with their own faction): name part = cost, comma separated. 0 or a missing name = not for hire.
How long a hire lasts, in in-game hours (24 = one day).
Reputation lost with the NPC's faction when your hired help dies.
Metres the follower keeps behind you.
A follower this far behind you for a few seconds (walls, a car you drove off in) pops back next to you. 0 = never.
Small animals the follower will not go hunting on its own (comma separated name parts). It still fights them if they hurt you.
The follower gives up a fight and comes back when its target is further than this many metres from you. 0 = no limit.
In the car, let the follower's own Detection/Attack/Damage Ranged chain shoot, as it does on foot. The mod's ShotDamage is only a backup for when that chain does not fire.
Play the follower's whole shooting animation on each shot from the car. Off by default: it lifts his arms over Apocapatrol's aiming pose. The muzzle flash is shown on its own instead.
How far a follower's gun arm kicks up on each shot from the car (degrees). 0 = no recoil.
Normally a follower's magazine size comes from the player's version of the gun he holds. Name=shots pairs here override it (e.g. Gunnar=20).
Normally a follower's reload time comes from the reload animation of the player's version of his gun. Name=seconds pairs here override it (e.g. Bolter=2).
Whose reload sounds a follower uses when his gun is not recognised (Name=player weapon, e.g. akm_trash, slamberg_500, crossbow). Others use the sounds of the player's version of the gun they hold.
Damage of each shot a follower fires from the car (the mod delivers the hit itself, because the follower's own sensors cannot see your enemies). 0 = no damage.
Seconds between a follower's shots from the car.
Hirable people who shoot from the car even though their ranged parts are not recognised (comma separated name parts). Gunnar, Pistoleer and Lugger are found automatically.

Apocapatrol only has gun-arm poses for its own humans (Boltjaw, Flexa, Lugnut, Scrud, Sprokka, Scraffa, Spanna). A ranged follower borrows the pose of this one so its arms aim and shoot. Use Name=Template pairs for different people, e.g. Gunnar=Scrud,Pistoleer=Lugnut; a lone name applies to everyone.
When you get in a car, a follower within this many metres gets in too.
Fetch quests also count matching items lying on the ground within this many metres of you.
Cans and other containers only count for fetch quests when they are at least this full (0.5 = half). 0 = any amount, even empty.
Kill jobs: bodies of the kills count when they lie within this many metres of the giver as you report in.
Kill jobs: bringing a body back to the giver adds this fraction of the reward for each body (0.10 = 10%), up to the number of kills asked for. Without bodies you get the normal reward. 0 = off.
Enemy deaths farther than this from you are ignored.
Kill quests only target enemies within this many metres of the giver, and only kills inside that area count. 0 = anywhere. Hand-written quests can override it with 'range'.
Show this mod in the Apocasetter Mods menu
After you take a job from an NPC, or turn one down, that NPC has no new job for you for this many in-game days (sleeping counts). 1 = one day. 0 = no limit.

A fetch quest is only offered when at least that many of the item exist within this many metres of the giver (items in the loaded part of the world, your own and the ones lying around; merchant stock never counts). 0 = no check.
Every job except a delivery has a time limit of at least this many in-game hours (24 = one day). When it runs out the job fails and costs FailPenalty reputation.
Added to the time limit for every km between the giver and the target (go-to, camp and talk jobs).
The most time any job is given (hand-written jobs with an hours = line may go over it).
An NPC will not offer the same quest (same camp, same enemy kind, same item...) that another NPC within this many metres has offered recently. 0 = off.
How long (in-game hours) an offered quest counts as taken for the neighbours.
A step of a quest chain (hand-written quests with chain / after) is always offered by an NPC that may give it, unless a different NPC offered that same step within this many in-game hours.
How close you must be (metres) to where you last saw a quest giver for them to be brought back if they are gone.
Reputation lost with the giver's faction when a delivery runs out of time (you kept the goods).

When a job fails (its time limit runs out) or you give it up, you lose this many times the reputation it would have given you for finishing it (at least 1). 0 = no penalty. A giver who dies costs nothing.

At or below this reputation (a negative number, the scale is -100 to +100) a faction's people turn hostile to you (the game's own PlayerIsEnemy switch). 0 = never (the default): bad reputation only lowers the pay. Factions always give work, whatever your reputation.
Bad reputation creeps back by 1 every this many in-game hours. 0 = never.
Jobs for a faction pay this fraction more for every point of positive reputation with it, and this fraction less for every negative point (0.005 = 0.5%). 0 = reputation does not change the pay.
Bad reputation never cuts the pay below this fraction of the normal reward.
Good reputation never raises the pay above this many times the normal reward. 0 = no limit.
Nuts you pay for 1 reputation point.
Nuts you get for selling 1 reputation point.
The most reputation one 'all' button buys or sells at a time.
Names of the NPCs who trade reputation (part of the name is enough, comma separated). They trade the reputation of the faction they belong to; an NPC with no faction does not.
Kills of the camp's people within this many metres of the camp count towards a takeover quest.
Generated takeover quests pick camps at least this far from the giver.
Generated takeover quests pick camps at most this far from the giver.
How many of the camp's people you must kill (generated takeover quests).
After the camp is cleared, the winning faction's people appear about this far from it and walk in.
How many people walk in.
If they have not arrived after this long, they are placed at the camp.
When you come near a camp you took and none of its new owner's people are there, this many of them are created. 0 = off.
How close you must be (metres) for an empty camp you took to get its garrison.
When one of a camp's garrison is killed while you are near, the camp is not refilled for this many in-game hours.
A camp's head count is only known once you are this close (metres); the quest log is updated then.
People who moved into a camp you took walk around it a little. Off = they stand where they arrive.
0 = the voice plays flat in your ears (best for dialogue), 1 = it comes from the NPC and gets quieter with distance.
